slides.title: When user input runs on your Node server
slides.summary: SSJI is XSS on the server: user data reaches eval or a similar sink and runs with your server's privileges.
body: Node.js powers SSR frameworks, BFFs and build tools. If user input reaches a function that evaluates code, the attacker runs JavaScript on the server: reading files, environment variables and secrets, or starting processes.

ul: NoSQL queries built from raw request objects ({ "$where": "…" }).

body: <mark>Never evaluate user input as code. There is no safe way to sanitize JavaScript.</mark>

slides.title: Related server-side injections
slides.summary: Prototype pollution and command injection follow the same pattern: untrusted data steering code.

ul: Prototype pollution: merging untrusted JSON like {"__proto__": {"isAdmin": true}} into objects changes every object in the process. Use Object.create(null), Map, or schema-validated objects, and keep merge libraries updated.
Command injection: use execFile / spawn with an argument array instead of exec with a string.
NoSQL injection: validate types so { "$gt": "" } can't arrive where a string was expected.

body.note: Run Node with the least privilege it needs, and consider Node's permission model (--permission) to restrict file system and child process access.
